description: Machine-readable security and privacy policy for AI-Vault. The checks in scripts/compliance/ read this file; changing a threshold here changes what blocks a pull request, so every relaxation must be an entry under `exceptions` with an owner, a justification and an expiry.

network.note: Every host the plugin may contact. Anything reachable from src/ that is not listed here is treated as undisclosed network use (OBS-POL-008) and fails.

allowedHosts.purpose: OpenAI chat completions, the Responses API and text embeddings for the RAG index.
allowedHosts.triggeredBy: A chat message sent with the OpenAI provider selected, or RAG indexing while an OpenAI key is configured.

allowedHosts.purpose: Anthropic Messages API, including server-side web search when the user enables it.
allowedHosts.triggeredBy: A chat message sent with the Anthropic provider selected.

userConfiguredHost.purpose: OpenAI-compatible or Ollama server chosen by the user. The plugin ships no default beyond loopback addresses.
userConfiguredHost.note: The host is whatever the user types. It is therefore not allowlisted; it is governed by the URL rules below and disclosed in PRIVACY.md.

forbiddenIndicators.note: Hostnames and SDK identifiers that would indicate telemetry or analytics. Presence in src/ or in the built bundle fails OBS-POL-004.

urlRules.note: Implemented and unit tested in src/security/urlPolicy.ts. This block is the declarative statement of the same rules so a reviewer can diff intent against code.

plainHttpAllowedWithoutWarningFor.note: Matching is exact. A hostname that merely contains the substring 'localhost' (localhost.attacker.example, notlocalhost) is remote. 'sub.localhost' is deliberately treated as remote too: RFC 6761 reserves it for loopback but resolution is resolver-dependent, and the safe default for a security control is to warn.

remotePlainHttp.rationale: Running a model server on another machine on the LAN is a legitimate, deliberate setup, so it is not blocked. It is warned about because chat messages, note excerpts, RAG chunks and the Local API key travel unencrypted.

embeddedCredentials.rationale: user:password@host in the Base URL leaks the credential into logs, error messages and settings backups.

storage.note: Files the plugin writes outside the Obsidian vault. Disclosed under OBS-POL-009.

files.name: keys.json
files.contains: OpenAI, Anthropic and Local API keys

files.name: projects.json
files.contains: project names, descriptions and custom system prompts

files.name: rag-index.json
files.contains: note chunks and their embedding vectors

rules: Every path segment must be a plain relative segment: no '..', no '.', no absolute path, no UNC path, no drive letter, no NUL byte.
Every resolved path must remain inside the configured base directory after normalization.
A rejected path refuses the operation. It never silently falls back to the base directory.

npmAudit.note: Scope is 'all' rather than production-only on purpose: this plugin has no runtime npm dependencies, so a production-only audit would always be empty and would prove nothing. Dev-tool findings are still real supply-chain exposure for anyone who builds or releases the plugin.

secretScan.note: Any credential-shaped string outside the declared fixture allowlist blocks the run.

licensePolicy.note: Only devDependencies exist today and none of them is bundled into main.js, but a copyleft build tool still creates obligations worth knowing about.

installScripts.note: Packages with install/preinstall/postinstall scripts are inventoried and reported. CI installs with --ignore-scripts where a build does not need them; esbuild's postinstall is required for its native binary and is the one accepted exception.

bundlePolicy.note: The release bundle is minified, which is expected and is not obfuscation. Anything in the bundle that has no counterpart in src/ is a finding.

exceptions.justification: The advisory affects esbuild's development HTTP server (`esbuild serve`), which lets any website send requests to it and read the response. This repository never starts that server: `npm run dev` uses esbuild's watch context and `npm run build` performs a one-shot rebuild, neither of which opens a port. esbuild is a build-time devDependency and is not bundled into main.js. Upgrading to 0.28.x is a bundler major bump that changes the bytes of main.js, which would break byte-for-byte reproducibility against the already published 1.1.1 artifact, so it is scheduled as a deliberate release-time change rather than a drive-by fix.
exceptions.onExpiry: The exception stops applying and the finding is reported at its natural severity. Moderate is below the blocking threshold, so this does not block a release either way; the expiry exists to force a re-decision.

exceptions.justification: The redaction tests and the compliance fixtures must contain credential-shaped strings in order to prove that redaction works. Every such literal is synthetic and contains the marker 'EXAMPLENOTAREALKEY' or 'NOTAREALSECRET'. The secret scanner requires that marker; any credential-shaped string in these paths without it still fails.
exceptions.onExpiry: Re-confirm that the fixtures still contain no real credential.
